purpose: Perform single-line literal substring search strictly within canonical Python files present in the current LIVE state.
parameters: search_term (string or null, optional, default null): single-line literal substring; newline (\n) and carriage return (\r) are invalid input; no regex, fuzzy, semantic or vector matching.
limit (positive integer or null, default 20): maximum logical matches returned; null returns all matches in canonical Python scope. max_items is not an alias for limit.
case_sensitive (boolean, default false): false uses Unicode casefold matching; true requires exact casing.
allow_large_output (boolean, default false): approve output above 15360 UTF-8 bytes after confirmation preflight.
query (string or null, optional, default null): alias for search_term. At least one of search_term or query must be supplied; when both are supplied, they must match exactly.
behavior: Only canonical Python modules are enumerated; excluded and non-canonical files are never walked or searched.
Matches are strict line-by-line literal substring occurrences, preserving exact match line numbers and 1-based start/end character spans.
Exact-offset line maps are provided for single-match results to support deterministic caller expansion.

The output guard enforces a 15360 UTF-8 byte threshold: when output exceeds 15360 bytes with allow_large_output=false, multi-match results are automatically bounded in a single shot to the largest deterministic match prefix fitting within 15360 bytes (returning _output.auto_bounded=true with full_output_bytes, requested_count, and returned_count). If a single match alone exceeds 15360 bytes, compact confirmation_required is returned.
Read-only query tool; never modifies repository or LIVE state.
errors: Returns invalid_search_term for empty search strings or strings containing newline characters.
Returns controlled error if neither search_term nor query is provided, or if they do not match exactly when both are supplied.
usage_notes: Prefer search_artifacts for symbol, artifact, and dependency queries; use search_source solely for literal text occurrences in Python source files.
When _output.auto_bounded is true or confirmation_required is returned, inspect full_output_bytes and repeat the query with allow_large_output=true to receive the complete requested match set.
